The GrowthCred field guide

ChatGPT, POPIA and private AI in South Africa. Private AI does not make you compliant. Map your data first.

Private AI or a paid ChatGPT plan does not make you POPIA-compliant on its own.

Keeping processing on local equipment can reduce some exposure. But you still need lawful purpose, data limits, and human checks.

Quick answer

Private AI does not make you POPIA-compliant. A paid ChatGPT plan does not either.

3 min read

You'll learn

  1. How to map information, purpose, access, and retention before choosing a private AI setup
  2. What on-premise processing changes under POPIA and what still requires governance and legal review

1You start with the information, purpose, and connected tools first

The problem

  1. Buying hardware or tools first ignores personal information.
  2. Confidentiality duties in client files. Unchecked connected tools, storage,. Access can pull in data your task never needed.

The way through

  1. You list the information in the task.
  2. Its lawful purpose, who may use it, and connected tools. Strip unnecessary data, set access. Retention rules, and name who checks outputs.

Map the information and the workflow before you deploy.

2What private AI changes, and why location alone is not enough for you

The problem

  1. Sending files to outside AI tools creates one set of exposure risks.
  2. Local equipment is not automatically safe if permissions are weak. Backups are unsafe, or workflows leak.

The way through

  1. Use private equipment inside your business.
  2. You want local control over processing and retention. Audit permissions, backups, and workflow design across your whole setup. Not just hardware location.

Private is a design choice. Compliance is your work around it.

3What POPIA and human oversight still ask of your team

The problem

  1. POPIA sections 19 to 22 require reasonable safeguards.
  2. Operator agreements, while section 72 covers cross-border transfers. Connected tools, support, backups. Or people can still move data or produce flawed outputs.

The way through

  1. Review operator terms, trace every data route including section 72 transfers.
  2. And have your lawyer check workflows. You keep a human responsible to review outputs. Anything reaches a client or changes a record.

You keep a human responsible for outputs. They reach a client or record.

Ask for a quote

4You run a safe test on sample data before real records

The problem

  1. Testing a new workflow directly on live client files risks exposure.
  2. Controls are proven. Controls can drift if underlying data, tools. Or workflows change later without rechecking.

The way through

  1. You test one recurring task on sample data without personal information.
  2. Then get sign-off before approved data. Record chosen controls, measure improvements,. Recheck them whenever data or workflows change.

You start with a sample without personal information. And get sign-off before approved data.
